question: The work done by a variable force is given by which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __W=∫F dx__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The work done by a variable force is determined by integrating the force over the displacement.
 
• In mathematical terms, it is expressed as W=∫F dx, where F is the force and dx is the infinitesimal displacement.
 
• This formula accounts for changes in force at different positions.
 
• Unlike constant force, variable force requires the use of integration to calculate work done.
 
• It is a fundamental concept in physics and is widely used in analyzing systems with non-uniform forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Work done by constant force:**
 
 
• When the force is constant, work is given by W = F·d·cosθ.
 
• Here, θ is the angle between the force and displacement vectors.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Energy and Work:**
 
 
• Work done on an object is directly related to its change in kinetic energy.
 
• The work-energy theorem states W = Δ(1/2 mv²).
